predecessors.name: Donghu
predecessors.text: the Donghu, who 'splintered into the Wuhuan and Xianbei' around 208 BC after the Xiongnu defeat; the Xianbei kept the Liao-Xing'an steppe

successors.name: Tuoba Xianbei
successors.text: the Tuoba, who 'in 258 ... settled near the frontier and occupied the abandoned city of Shengle' (near modern Hohhot), after Tuoba Liwei in 248

successors.name: Murong Xianbei
successors.text: the Murong, who 'assisted the Cao Wei dynasty in ending the control of the Gongsun warlords in Liaodong in 238'; the page gives no land for them in 235; the strip without the Southern Xiongnu's land

successors.name: Duan Liaoxi
successors.text: the Duan, founded by 'a Xianbei ex-slave of the Wuhuan' in Liaoxi Commandery (undated)

successors.name: Yuwen Xianbei
successors.text: the Yuwen, who 'began living between the Luan River and Liucheng' (undated)

ledger.x: 49: the Xianbei chieftain Pianhe, urged by the Han governor Ji Tong, turns on the Xiongnu.
87: the Xianbei kill the Xiongnu chanyu Youliu.
91: the fighting for the plateau ends.
91: the Xianbei occupy the Mongolian Plateau.
151: Dzungaria passes from the last Northern Xiongnu to the Xianbei, or to no one, when the remnant vanishes.
156: Tanshihuai takes the Xianbei in hand and holds court at Mount Danhan.
197: the Xianbei break into many groups.
205: Kuitou dies and his domain is divided.
235: Kebineng is assassinated and the Xianbei no longer act as one.

wars.name: Xianbei-Xiongnu war
wars.outcome: Xianbei and Han victory: the chanyu Youliu killed in 87, the Northern Xiongnu beaten by Han in 89 and 91, the plateau occupied by the Xianbei from 91.

wars.name: Xianbei raids on Han China
wars.outcome: Raids without lasting territory: Wuyuan Commandery 109; Qizhijian four raids 121-138; Dai Commandery 145; Tanshihuai from 156 (Yunzhong, nine border commanderies in 166 with the Southern Xiongnu and Wuhuan, Jiuquan in 178); the Han counterattack of 177 lost…

wars.name: Kebineng's wars of consolidation
wars.outcome: Kebineng killed Fuluohan in 218 and Budugen by 233 and was assassinated by a Wei agent in 235; the brothers' share of Kuitou's divided domain is the ground at stake (zone), and passes to Kebineng's confederation in 233 (ledger 233).

certainty.note: A nomad confederation: every frontier is approximate; no treaty or survey line appears on the pages opened.
